note: RV park beside I-49 at Archie, south of Kansas City (213 NW Outer Rd), with tent sites and a pondside cabin; propane delivered to the site. It also sells monthly and extended stays, aimed at travel nurses and work crews. --Claude
summary: Private park selling single nights on RoverPass ($48.93-51.50 cheapest RV site, up to $64.50); own site lists $39+ nightly/$250+ weekly/$550+ monthly with dynamic pricing. Strong workforce/extended-stay side: on a November weeknight 48 of ~137 RV sites were open vs 133 in June 2027. Borderline on the $50 gate (Signature $51.50 in November). Phone matches. Flags for AWH: price and long-stay share.
flags: PRICE (borderline, $50 gate): the cheapest one-night RV site a 23-ft rig fits is Signature at $48.93 (January and June 2027 dates) but $51.50 on 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-21 (dynamic pricing); the $39-44.50 'Standard' rate needs 7 nights, so the page's 'Nightly: $39+' is not a one-night price. RoverPass cart 2026-11-17: Signature $51.50 + RoverPass platform $3.50 + processing $1.80 (platform fees not counted). No gateway within 40 km (Kansas City 71 km). Google 4.2/184 is decent, so reviews don't push it either way. Stored fees 39/39 replaced (no human provenance).

LONG-STAY TESTS (AWH 2026-10-14): (1) price at the line: $48.93 most dates, $51.50 in November, see PRICE; (2) one night sold on RoverPass with no application; the rules require management approval for RVs 10+ years old (a 2023 rig passes) and the monthly page asks for RV year/length/setup for extended stays only; pass; (3) no minimum on the nightly rates (only Standard needs 7), pass; (4) nightly-rate sites: 44 open on Tue 2026-11-17 and 103 on 2027-06-08 (Signature 48, Signature PLUS 1, Premium 12, Premium PLUS 42; another 30 Standard sites need 7 nights), so far over 1 in 10, pass; (5) not a home community (no homes or lots sold), pass.

LONG-TERM SHARE / OCCUPANCY: RV inventory ~137 sites (103 nightly + 30 Standard + K-13 etc., rows A-N). On Tue 2026-11-17 only 48 RV sites were open (44 nightly + 4 Standard) against 133 open on 2027-06-08 and 128 on 2027-01-26, so ~85 sites (~60%) were taken on a November weeknight, most likely by extended-stay guests. The park markets monthly/extended stays to 'travel nurses; construction, utility and pipeline crews; commuters; and families between homes', and its rules read residential (heated hose required by November 1, skirting approval, sewer-support ladder for extended stays, no deep freezers/window units/homesteading). A '*NEW* Premium' build-out shows nightly sites being added. So: a workforce-heavy park that still sells a large nightly block; by the nightly count it passes test 4 comfortably. Review text could not be read (Google's signed-out view showed only the summary); the topic chips were highway noise 7, gravel roads 9, fishing pond 5, quiet rv park 5, after-hours check-in 4. Decision for AWH: keep on test 4, or drop as mostly long-term + borderline price (the 'on the fence = drop' rule of 2026-10-31 would drop it if this reads iffy).
